title: PowerPoint on the web: attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, image-attachment workflow, licence-assignment controls and connected-experience requirements match Microsoft's sources. It distinguishes general Copilot licensing and controls from the narrower image-specific details Microsoft has not published.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes referencing an image when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint for the web can use a user-attached image during presentation creation.
claims.quote:
Attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows, Web, Mac]
Copilot in PowerPoint now allows users to reference attached images during presentation creation.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate administrator setting for image attachment in Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot image attachment administrator disable policy; PowerPoint attach image policy disable; PowerPoint image Copilot Graph setting. Read release notes, requirements and connected-experience guidance; results cover other image features, not an attachment switch.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Licence assignment is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page.
Select a product.
On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: licence assignment
claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: licence assignment
claims.claim: The documented assignment control governs licence entitlement, not a separate image-attachment toggle.
claims.quote: You can assign or unassign licenses for users in the Microsoft 365 admin center on either the Active users page, or on the Licenses page.

claims.where: Governance controls: privacy page
claims.claim: The privacy page says disabling connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot unavailable in PowerPoint on the devices it describes.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
Excel
OneNote
Outlook
PowerPoint
Word

claims.where: Governance controls: privacy page device qualification
claims.claim: The privacy-page statement applies to the most current app versions on Windows, Mac, iOS or Android devices.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.where: Governance controls: privacy page web qualification
claims.claim: The privacy page does not name the web in that device-scope sentence.
claims.quote: Searched: analyze your content and Windows, Mac in the fetched privacy page; read surrounding paragraphs. Its scope sentence lists Windows, Mac, iOS and Android, not web. Separate sensitive-customer guidance explicitly covers web through Cloud Policy.

claims.where: Governance controls: sensitive and regulated customer guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft's sensitive and regulated customer guidance says Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category in Office to be enabled for Copilot to work in Microsoft 365 Apps, including Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: Governance controls: sensitive and regulated customer guidance
claims.claim: The connected-experience guidance says web experiences are controlled exclusively by Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: The web experiences and modern apps are controlled exclusively by the Cloud Policy.
